questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: In Vienna there are two options for studying psychology; Wien Universität (WU) and the private university Sigmund Freud University. I choose WU for academic reasons, since it's the superior university in this regard. Also the main building is one of the most beautiful buildings you'll ever see, and to get to study in that place.... What an experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The international office at the main building was very qualified in helping with whatever problem you could think of. I didn't really reach out to them before getting the certificate of departure, but everyone I know got the help they needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned before, I didn't need help in the beginning of my stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used AirBNB the hole stay, which only made sense because i travelled with my girlfriend and we had two incomes. I you travel alone I can recommend WG-Gesucht as a very student friendly platform for housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You have to figure it out on your own, but that shouldn't come as a surprise.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Oh wow, what a stressful event. Before departing from home, you'll have to register for every course you just have the slightest interest in, because you aren't secured a spot on any of the courses before the deadline of registration. So you'll need registration on backup-courses in the case - and this WILL happen - you don't get offered a spot on the ones you have made the "forhåndsgodkendelse" for. Another problem is that the courses for the semester are only made visible very close to the day of departure from home, so the hole thing seems very confusing. BUT everything will work out in the end, it's just not a very intelligent registration process as far as I'm concerned.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Everyone says the same thing, just register for a lot of different courses!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would say around 50% of the courses I took was in alignment with courses I had planned on taking beforehand.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience and always a large cup of coffee close at hand.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the courses were awesome and were taught at a very high level, others were forgettable and were structured horribly. For us psychology student we need to take many courses since they usually are around 4-5 ECTS points.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: A very wide range of good and bad courses; as you can expect from taking around 6-8 different courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some matched, others didn't.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Economic Psychology - Motivation in Work and Occupation, 2) Economic Psychology (another focus in this course), 3) Psychology of Work and Labour, 4) Environmental Psychology, 5) Slavoj Zizek and the Arts, and 6) SE Advanced Seminar: Mind and Brain - Meta-psychology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The teacher Filip Melinšcak is a champ, and gives very good lectures in generel. I took his course Meta-psychology which was awesome.

questions.answer: The prices aren't that much lower than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The city that offers literally everything.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many activities I believe, but I didn't really use them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Too many things to write about here. The city offers everything, and you need a least six months to get to experience just a fraction.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Too many things to write about here. The city offers everything, and you need a least six months to get to experience just a fraction.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the people of Vienna are warm and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hmm, you'll probably socialize primarily with other Erasmus students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Only the language, which I really can't complain about.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Its richness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) the city brewery Ottakringer makes a zwickl beer that is just out of this world, 2) if you like history and are culturally aware, then this is the city for you, and 3) you won't regret going here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, just leave already.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To end up being mistaken for a local myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To get time to try everything.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
